name: van Ophoven amitriptyline trial
question: Does oral amitriptyline improve interstitial cystitis symptoms more than placebo after four months?

design.population: Fifty patients (44 women and 6 men) meeting National Institute of Diabetes, Digestive and Kidney Diseases symptom criteria for interstitial cystitis.
design.description: Single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial; all participants had received prior conservative treatment and none had taken amitriptyline
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods and Table 1, pp 533–534

verdictNote: The primary symptom score favored amitriptyline; anticholinergic effects were common.
takeaway: In 48 evaluable patients with interstitial cystitis, four months of amitriptyline improved the O'Leary-Sant symptom/problem score more than placebo (mean change −8.4 versus −3.5; p = 0.005); anticholinergic effects occurred in 22/24 versus 5/24.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: August 2004; PubMed citation: 2004 Aug
reports.citation: van Ophoven A, Pokupic S, Heinecke A, Hertle L. "A prospective, randomized, placebo controlled, double-blind study of amitriptyline for the treatment of interstitial cystitis." *J Urol.* 2004;172(2):533-536. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000132388.54703.4d
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 534

results.endpoint: O'Leary-Sant IC symptom and problem index score
results.measure: Mean change from baseline to four months; between-arm mean difference in change
results.note: The −4.9-point between-arm difference is arithmetic; the reported P value is from a Mann-Whitney U test. No confidence interval is reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 534

results.measure: Visual analog scale changes at four months
results.note: Both between-arm comparisons had P <0.001; values are mean change ± SD.

results.measure: 48-hour voiding log change at four months
results.note: Mean change ± SD; between-arm comparison was not statistically significant.

results.measure: 48-hour voiding log change at four months
results.note: Mean change ± SD; between-arm comparison was not statistically significant.

results.measure: Patient Global Assessment after four months among completers
results.note: Good and excellent categories combined; the paper reports 63% and 4% after rounding.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table 3, p 534

harms.label: Anticholinergic side effects
harms.note: Reported among 24 evaluable patients per arm.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: Grade 1 mouth dryness; no grade 2 mouth dryness was reported.

harms.label: Withdrawal because of side effects
harms.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Results, p 534

harms.label: Grade 3 or higher adverse effects
harms.value: None reported in either arm; denominator for this statement not specified.
harms.note: Adverse effects were graded by Common Toxicity Criteria, not Clavien-Dindo.

delivery.label: Dose escalation and duration
delivery.value: Amitriptyline 25 mg at bedtime, escalating weekly to 50, 75 and at most 100 mg if not symptom-free; maintain the lowest dose giving satisfactory relief, for four months. Placebo followed the same protocol.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 534

delivery.label: Available for endpoint evaluation
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Results, p 534
delivery.note: Table 1 reports 25 randomized per arm; one patient per arm withdrew for adverse effects.

relations.note: The later treatment-naïve trial with behavioral care found no significant intention-to-treat global-response benefit.
